newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mostly weaker, vessels scarce.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mostly weaker, vessels scarce.

text.p: Med oil products were mostly weaker on Wednesday, with volumes hit by scarcity of vessels, traders said.

Naphtha was readily available and demand was seen, but the main problem was the difficulty of finding a tanker and the expense of chartering. Dealers said freight was around $15 a tonne. "I can find cargoes on a fob basis, but then it's almost impossible to get a ship," said one trader.
Prices were up to $4 lower, reflecting losses in NWE.
Gasoline was also easier, losing $2 or so as it tracked crude's weakness for much of the day.

Outright gas oil prices shed 25 cents a tonne on easier futures. Notional Russian heating oil rates were around cif Med quotes +$3/3.50 but volume was again very light, hampered by very tight shipping markets.
Black Sea to Med was offered around W235/240, with cross Med rates were steady at 330 and Med/NWE at 270. One trader said: "The ship owners have to come back to more reasonable levels."
Low sulphur fuel oil continued its slide and ended weaker even after crude futures regained earlier losses, traders said.
Dealers said at least 200,000 tonnes of low sulphur fuel oil was available to load in northwest Europe in the next 18 days.

Data from Italian trade grouping Unione Petrolifera showed Italy's power generation sector consumed 1.70 million tonnes of high and low sulphur fuel oil in December 1996, 17.7 percent lower than in December 1995.
A Turkish tender for 40-45,000 tonnes of low sulphur fuel oil was heard awarded to a trader.
A Syrian tender for two high sulphur cargoes was heard awarded to two other traders, one of whom was seen having fixed a vessel from the eastern Mediterranean to Senegal.
